beats.text: Bad night? You might push people away. Literally.
In one study, after a sleepless night, people stopped approaching strangers sooner.
They kept others about eighteen to sixty percent farther away.
And over a thousand online viewers, who didn't know, rated them as lonelier.
Even worse: watching them made the viewers feel a little lonelier themselves.
So before you decide nobody likes you, maybe just sleep.

sources: Ben Simon & Walker (2018). Sleep loss causes social withdrawal and loneliness. Nature Communications 9. 18 adults tested rested vs sleep-deprived: kept strangers 18-60% farther away; >1,000 online raters judged sleep-deprived people lonelier and less socially desirable; viewers felt more alienated after watching. Via UC Berkeley News.
